gas.note: Phase 7D (owner decisions 2026-11-04 and 2026-11-20): default utility supply priced in each utility's native billing unit. Residential levels since 7D-1; commercial general-service levels for two building sizes since 7D-2, each with a reference level and x0.5 and x2 sensitivity levels. A level is an average month: annual use = 12 x the level, which selects each utility's class (published annual limits) unless a peak_month_factors entry applies. The m3 and GJ tracks are never converted or merged; a future cross-unit comparison converts toward m3, with its heating-value source chosen then. Contract-demand, interruptible, seasonal and peaking classes are not modelled yet (owner decision 2026-11-20).

assumptions.usage_levels_basis: Monthly usage levels: electricity residential 500/1,000/2,000 kWh (approved October 9, 2026; 1,000 kWh is the reference level and 500/2,000 are sensitivity levels, owner decision November 20, 2026); commercial under 50 kW s1 = 2,000 kWh at 14 kW and s2 = 10,000 kWh at 40 kW (owner decision November 20, 2026, replacing 2,000 kWh at 10 kW and 8,000 kWh at 25 kW); 50-499 kW m1 = 40,000 kWh at 100 kW; 500-4,999 kW l1 = 500,000 kWh at 1,000 kW; no level yet for 5,000 kW and over. Gas levels are in the gas section (native m3 or GJ, residential and commercial). Each level records its decision, what it represents, why it was chosen and its sources (owner rule November 20, 2026). Daily charges convert to monthly at 30.4375 days (365.25 / 12); hours per month 730.5. kVA demand is derived from kW at the disclosed 0.9 power factor (kVA = kW / 0.9) and never treated as kW. Implied load factors (kWh / (kW x 730.5)): s1 19.6%, s2 34.2%, m1 54.8%, l1 68.4%. Levels are comparison points for modeled costs, not a load profile of any customer.

ON_RPP.method: Compute each usage level's monthly cost once per season with that season's tier threshold (and TOU hours), then month-weight: cost = (6 x winter + 6 x summer) / 12.

tiered_profile_reference.note: OEB assumed tiered load profile of the November 1, 2026 report (Table 2-ES page 6, Table 6 page 24, section 3.3 page 23; the November 1, 2025 report's Table 4 gave 64%/36%); informational only - usage-level costs apply the published thresholds directly.

source.location: Executive summary, 'Regulated Price Plan - Tiered Pricing' (page 6); TOU and ULO periods pages 5 and 22-23. Printed page numbers equal PDF page numbers in this report.
source.quote: The threshold for residential consumers changes twice a year on a seasonal basis: to 600 kWh per month during the summer season (May 1 to October 31) and to 1,000 kWh per month during the winter season (November 1 to April 30). The threshold for non-residential RPP consumers remains constant at 750 kWh per month for the entire year.

NT_TPSP.method: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) first block in the after-subsidy cost: compute each usage level's cost once per season with that season's first block at the stored Yellowknife-rate price, which is all-in (it replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh, riders and credits included: owner decisions 76 and 78), then month-weight: cost = (7 x September-March + 5 x April-August) / 12, as for Ontario's RPP tiers (ON_RPP). The engine checks every stored first-block threshold against first_block_kwh_per_month; a different threshold or months that do not cover the year once make the after-subsidy cost not computable.

source.title: Northwest Territories Power Corporation, Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP)
source.quote: From September 1 to March 31 each year, residential customers only pay the Yellowknife rate on the first 1,000 kilowatt hours (kWh) of power that they consume. After 1,000 kWh, each additional kilowatt hour is charged at the Zone Rate. From April 1 to August 31 – when there are more hours of daylight – residential customers pay the Yellowknife rate (where costs are lower) on the first 600 kilowatt hours -- after that, each additional kilowatt hour, is charged at the Zone Rate.

component_rules: Included: unconditional components in effect at the as-of date (fixed, energy, distribution, demand, transmission, regulatory, riders, carbon, other) in $/month, $/30 days, $/day, $/year, $/two months (/ 2), $/metering device/day (one metering device), $/kWh, $/MWh, $/kW, $/kVA (per month or per day), and gas in the model's own unit ($/m³ or $/GJ).

Included as reference-customer charges: conditional or optional components that a reviewed usage_levels.json 'reference_customer' entry lists for the province, fuel and sector (Ontario: Class B CBR, Standard Supply Service administration, non-wholesale-market-participant riders, and non-RPP Class B Global Adjustment riders at 50 kW and over; Quebec gas: Energir's renewable-gas socialization charges and its load balancing below 75,000 m³ a year; New Brunswick gas: Liberty Utility Gas supply), itemized with reason 'reference_customer:<id>'. An entry with an annual-volume limit makes the record not computable at levels outside it (Energir's load-factor formula price at 75,000 m³ a year or more).

Included as reference-customer fixed-charge variants: a fixed charge published as variants of one charge (unconditional variants or alternatives) is priced with the one variant that a usage_levels.json 'fixed_charge_variants' rule selects: by level (user decision 2026-10-30: homes single-phase 200 A service; small business single phase at s1 and three phase at s2, 14 and 40 kW since 7D-2), by the monthly peak of a peak_month_factors entry (Liberty's customer charges) or by the band containing 12 x the level's volume (annual-volume bands such as Energir's basic fee); itemized with reason 'fixed_charge_variant:<id>'.

Excluded and counted: other conditional components (sub_component 'conditional'/'conditional_credit' or notes starting 'Conditional'), alternatives, optional components, components expired (end_date before the as-of date) or not yet effective, value-less market energy (model state market_energy_pending), value-less market-indexed non-energy charges (named in the method; the state does not change) and percentage adjustments (no computable base) other than the reviewed ones below.

Percentage riders (owner decision 64, 2026-11-24): a percentage component with a reviewed data/models/percentage_riders.json entry is priced as its percentage of the base charges the entry names (never of other riders), itemized with reason 'percentage_rider:<id>'; reviewed percentages of the whole bill or of revenues billed are disclosed, not applied; reviewed percentage subsidies apply only in the after-subsidy cost. In the territories a percentage component without a reviewed entry makes its record not computable.

Territorial subsidies (owner decisions 67-70, 74 and 76-78, 2026-11-24): the cost before subsidies leaves subsidy prices and credits out; the after-subsidy cost (before tax only) applies only the automatic subsidies of data/models/subsidies.json and the reviewed percentage subsidies in force at the as-of date. Reference rates (GREP) and first-block prices (TPSP) are all-in: they replace the zone's whole tariff, or the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh; seasonal first blocks are priced per season and month-weighted.

Thresholds as published: demand charges with a demand threshold bill only the kW above it; demand and energy blocks use their published bounds (kVA bounds at the power factor; per-kW and per-kVA energy blocks scale with the level's demand; per-day blocks x days per month; a block published in bare 'kWh' only with the first matching reviewed entry of data/models/block_periods.json: month as published, two months / 2, day x days per month; a null period or no entry is not computable); an unseasoned first block applies in every season of the seasonal blocks that follow it.

Class selection: a record serves a level only when its published eligibility covers it: kW and kWh bounds for electricity; for gas, the reviewed crosswalk usage_bounds (12 x the level's monthly volume, or its monthly peak), else stored annual bounds (a level exactly on a stored bound is not computable without a reviewed entry). Elective classes of one utility (crosswalk elective_classes) count once, as the cheapest.

Not computable (record left out at that level, reason listed): a charge published only as conditional alternatives, fixed charges published as variants of one charge (e.g. by amperage or phase) when no usage_levels.json 'fixed_charge_variants' rule of the level selects exactly one variant, an unconditional component without value or in an unsupported unit (e.g. per billing period), TOU periods without an official share, ambiguous tier thresholds, seasons that do not cover the year, demand charges at a level without kW.
assumptions.reference_customer_basis: Conditional components are left out of modeled costs unless an entry below says that the reference (typical) customer of the sector pays them (user decision, October 9, 2026). An entry applies to components of its province and fuel, for the listed sectors (residential or a commercial size band), whose notes (after the 'Provenance: ...' prefix) fully match notes_regex and whose component name fully matches name_regex (Python re.fullmatch; every given pattern must match). Only components otherwise excluded as 'conditional' qualify: alternatives, optional components, expired or not-yet-effective components and value-less market components stay excluded. Included components are itemized with reason 'reference_customer:<id>'. Ontario reference customers: residential and GS < 50 kW customers are on the Regulated Price Plan (RPP) and buy from their distributor (standard supply); customers at the 50 kW and over levels buy spot-priced energy through their distributor (non-RPP standard supply); all are Class B (not Industrial Conservation Initiative participants) and none is a wholesale market participant. Still excluded: the Hydro One RRRP credit (principal-residence condition), EV charging rates, former Chapleau PUC rider sets, transformer-ownership allowances, primary-metering and transformer-loss allowances, and meter-type, interval-meter and demand-size alternatives.

assumptions.fixed_charge_variants_basis: A fixed charge published as variants of one charge, either as unconditional variants such as 'Basic Customer Charge (Single Phase)' / 'Basic Customer Charge (Three Phase)', as alternatives marked 'Alternative: applies ...', or as bands of annual volume of which one applies, is priced for the reference customer of the usage level. Rules select by level (user decision, October 30, 2026: homes are single-phase service of 200 A; small businesses are single-phase at s1 and three-phase at s2, now 14 kW and 40 kW, owner decision 2026-11-20), by the level's monthly peak (a 'peak_month' range tested on the level x its peak_month_factors entry: Liberty Gas NB customer charges, owner decision 17, 2026-11-20) or by annual-volume band ('select': 'annual_volume_band': the band whose published annual window strictly contains 12 x the level; Energir's basic fee per metering device, owner decision 8, 2026-11-20). A rule applies to its fuel, sectors and, when given, province, utility and tariff_code; the variant whose component name fully matches match.name_regex (Python re.fullmatch) is priced. Exactly one matching variant with a value per month is priced and itemized with reason 'fixed_charge_variant:<id>'; no match or more than one leaves the record not computable at that level with the existing reason.

percentage_riders.status: Reviewed percentage riders of the representative models (owner decision 64, 2026-11-24). Each entry quotes the official text that says what the percentage applies to. Treatments: 'apply' prices the rider as its percentage of the charges named by 'base' (base charges only, never other riders); 'exclude' keeps a percentage of the whole bill or of revenues billed disclosed but not applied; 'subsidy' is an automatic percentage rebate, left out of the cost before subsidies and applied only in the after-subsidy figure while its component dates are in force (data/models/subsidies.json). The engine requires a reviewed entry for every percentage component of a territorial (YT, NT, NU) record: a percentage component without one makes that record not computable. Provincial percentage adjustments stay disclosed and not applied; there are no provincial entries.
percentage_riders.rule: An entry matches a component of a record of its utility when match.component_name_regex (and, when given, match.tariff_code_regex) fully match. Base: the record's priced charges whose component names fully match base.component_name_regex, at the usage level (percentage riders never apply to each other). A 'subsidy' entry may name the 'apply' riders whose share of the base it also covers (with_riders) and a monthly kWh limit, which must equal the component's published threshold.

subsidies.status: Reviewed territorial subsidies of the representative models (owner decisions 67-70, 74 and 76-78, 2026-11-24).
subsidies.rule: Territorial models show each level's cost before subsidies (the published tariff: subsidy prices are stored as conditional alternatives or conditional credits and stay out of it) and, where 'jurisdictions' allows it, the cost after the automatic subsidies below (treatments reference_rates, first_block_price and per_kwh_credit) and the 'subsidy' entries of data/models/percentage_riders.json. A subsidy counts as automatic only where an official source says so (decision 67): an applied program quotes that text in 'automatic'. Reference rates replace the whole tariff of the zone records they apply to ('applies_to'), every charge and rider (decision 78); a first-block price replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh in the tariff in force, riders and credits included (decisions 76 and 78); a per-kWh credit with within_first_block false applies to the kWh above the first block. Programs with treatment 'disclose' are named, never applied. A subsidy whose price is not stored for a zone record is not applied there and is named (with its reviewed 'absent' reason when one is given), so the after-subsidy cost never claims a subsidy that the sources do not establish; a zone record that a reference-rate program applies to but whose reference rates are missing is not computable after subsidies. Seasonal first blocks are priced once per season and month-weighted (decision 68; usage_levels.json seasons). After-subsidy figures are published before tax only (decision 74).
subsidies.tax_note: After-subsidy costs are shown before tax only, until bills or official text confirm the GST base on subsidised bills (owner decision 74, 2026-11-24). The with-tax figures are computed on the cost before subsidies, as for the provinces.

commercial.reason: No automatic subsidy for general service: the Yukon Affordability Rate Relief is for the 'Residential - Non Government customer class only. Not applicable to any commercial, industrial or government customers.' (Affordability Rate Relief Rebate, effective 2026 10 01). The commercial models show the cost before subsidies only.

No after-subsidy cost is computed for general service. The GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy also applies automatically to commercial customers (NTPC, February 2026 Rider Explanation: 'This credit automatically applies to all eligible residential and commercial customers, including local governments (Hamlets, Towns, Bands).'), but NTPC publishes no credit value for general service: none is printed in its rate schedule effective June 1, 2026 (https://www.ntpc.com/sites/default/files/2026-06/NTPC%20Rate%20Schedule%20-%20June%201%202026.pdf), on its residential rates page or on its business-service pages (read 2026-11-24), and the stored general service records carry none. TPSP is for residential customers only. Naka's GREP general-service reference rates apply only in its Thermal zone, whose general service is not stored.

programs.quote: Their TPSP program ensures that all NWT households can, with modest energy saving efforts, pay the same low power rate as Yellowknife. From September 1 to March 31 each year, residential customers only pay the Yellowknife rate on the first 1,000 kilowatt hours (kWh) of power that they consume. After 1,000 kWh, each additional kilowatt hour is charged at the Zone Rate.
programs.location: Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) page (read 2026-11-24); first-block prices: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026 (https://www.ntpc.com/customer-service/residential-service/residential-electrical-rates), 'Your cost' column
programs.evidence: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026: under 'Up to 1000 kWh' the 'Your cost' column lists only 'Energy charge 36.50 cents / kWh', and the riders and the GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy are listed only under 'Each additional kWh' (Thermal: 84.68 = 88.96 + 1.01 + 7.72 + 0.42 - 13.43 cents). The page's saving statements are consistent with an all-in block: 'If you use 1000 kWh, you save $524.60 per month -- that's the amount paid by the GNWT Territorial Power Support Program.' ($524.60 = 1,000 kWh x (88.96 - 36.50) cents in the Thermal zone; Norman Wells $348.00 = 1,000 x (71.30 - 36.50) cents): they equal the energy-charge difference because no rider is listed on the first-block kWh in either column ('Your cost' and 'Actual cost'). Naka's July 2026 rate-update notice shows the same program's first block all-in.
programs.note: The first-block price is all-in (owner decision 76, 2026-11-24): the first-block kWh pay 36.50 cents in place of the energy charge, NTPC's per-kWh riders and the Cost of Living credit; the monthly service charge stays. TPSP is omitted and disclosed in the Snare zone (owner decision 77); NTPC publishes no TPSP price for Fort Resolution, Fort Smith and Hay River, whose after-subsidy cost has the Cost of Living credit on every kWh.

subsidies.tax_note: After-subsidy costs are shown before tax only, until bills or official text confirm the GST base on subsidised bills (owner decision 74, 2026-11-24). The with-tax figures are computed on the cost before subsidies, as for the provinces.
subsidies.rule: Territorial models show each level's cost before subsidies (the published tariff: subsidy prices are stored as conditional alternatives or conditional credits and stay out of it) and, where 'jurisdictions' allows it, the cost after the automatic subsidies below (treatments reference_rates, first_block_price and per_kwh_credit) and the 'subsidy' entries of data/models/percentage_riders.json. A subsidy counts as automatic only where an official source says so (decision 67): an applied program quotes that text in 'automatic'. Reference rates replace the whole tariff of the zone records they apply to ('applies_to'), every charge and rider (decision 78); a first-block price replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh in the tariff in force, riders and credits included (decisions 76 and 78); a per-kWh credit with within_first_block false applies to the kWh above the first block. Programs with treatment 'disclose' are named, never applied. A subsidy whose price is not stored for a zone record is not applied there and is named (with its reviewed 'absent' reason when one is given), so the after-subsidy cost never claims a subsidy that the sources do not establish; a zone record that a reference-rate program applies to but whose reference rates are missing is not computable after subsidies. Seasonal first blocks are priced once per season and month-weighted (decision 68; usage_levels.json seasons). After-subsidy figures are published before tax only (decision 74).

programs.name: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP)
programs.replaces: the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh: the energy charge, NTPC's per-kWh riders and the GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy (the first-block price is all-in, owner decision 76); the monthly service charge stays, and the riders and the credit apply to the kWh above the block

seasons.method: GNWT Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) first block in the after-subsidy cost: compute each usage level's cost once per season with that season's first block at the stored Yellowknife-rate price, which is all-in (it replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh, riders and credits included: owner decisions 76 and 78), then month-weight: cost = (7 x September-March + 5 x April-August) / 12, as for Ontario's RPP tiers (ON_RPP). The engine checks every stored first-block threshold against first_block_kwh_per_month; a different threshold or months that do not cover the year once make the after-subsidy cost not computable.

automatic.quote: Residential customers are automatically enrolled in the Territorial Power Support Program when they set up their household account. Customers can only have one TPSP account at any given time.

programs.quote: Their TPSP program ensures that all NWT households can, with modest energy saving efforts, pay the same low power rate as Yellowknife. From September 1 to March 31 each year, residential customers only pay the Yellowknife rate on the first 1,000 kilowatt hours (kWh) of power that they consume. After 1,000 kWh, each additional kilowatt hour is charged at the Zone Rate.
programs.location: Territorial Power Support Program (TPSP) page (read 2026-11-24); first-block prices: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026 (https://www.ntpc.com/customer-service/residential-service/residential-electrical-rates), 'Your cost' column
programs.evidence: Residential Electrical Rates, effective September 1, 2026: under 'Up to 1000 kWh' the 'Your cost' column lists only 'Energy charge 36.50 cents / kWh', and the riders and the GNWT Cost of Living Subsidy are listed only under 'Each additional kWh' (Thermal: 84.68 = 88.96 + 1.01 + 7.72 + 0.42 - 13.43 cents). The page's saving statements are consistent with an all-in block: 'If you use 1000 kWh, you save $524.60 per month -- that's the amount paid by the GNWT Territorial Power Support Program.' ($524.60 = 1,000 kWh x (88.96 - 36.50) cents in the Thermal zone; Norman Wells $348.00 = 1,000 x (71.30 - 36.50) cents): they equal the energy-charge difference because no rider is listed on the first-block kWh in either column ('Your cost' and 'Actual cost'). Naka's July 2026 rate-update notice shows the same program's first block all-in.
programs.note: The first-block price is all-in (owner decision 76, 2026-11-24): the first-block kWh pay 36.50 cents in place of the energy charge, NTPC's per-kWh riders and the Cost of Living credit; the monthly service charge stays. TPSP is omitted and disclosed in the Snare zone (owner decision 77); NTPC publishes no TPSP price for Fort Resolution, Fort Smith and Hay River, whose after-subsidy cost has the Cost of Living credit on every kWh.

subsidies.tax_note: After-subsidy costs are shown before tax only, until bills or official text confirm the GST base on subsidised bills (owner decision 74, 2026-11-24). The with-tax figures are computed on the cost before subsidies, as for the provinces.
subsidies.rule: Territorial models show each level's cost before subsidies (the published tariff: subsidy prices are stored as conditional alternatives or conditional credits and stay out of it) and, where 'jurisdictions' allows it, the cost after the automatic subsidies below (treatments reference_rates, first_block_price and per_kwh_credit) and the 'subsidy' entries of data/models/percentage_riders.json. A subsidy counts as automatic only where an official source says so (decision 67): an applied program quotes that text in 'automatic'. Reference rates replace the whole tariff of the zone records they apply to ('applies_to'), every charge and rider (decision 78); a first-block price replaces the whole per-kWh price of the first-block kWh in the tariff in force, riders and credits included (decisions 76 and 78); a per-kWh credit with within_first_block false applies to the kWh above the first block. Programs with treatment 'disclose' are named, never applied. A subsidy whose price is not stored for a zone record is not applied there and is named (with its reviewed 'absent' reason when one is given), so the after-subsidy cost never claims a subsidy that the sources do not establish; a zone record that a reference-rate program applies to but whose reference rates are missing is not computable after subsidies. Seasonal first blocks are priced once per season and month-weighted (decision 68; usage_levels.json seasons). After-subsidy figures are published before tax only (decision 74).
